title: In re Lisa Motley, Case No. 26-007C (Former LV Convention & Visitors Authority VP of Sports & Special Events)
text:
STATE OF NEVADA
BEFORE THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
In re Lisa Motley, Ethics Complaint
Former Vice President of Sports and Case No. 26-007C
Special Events, Las Vegas Convention
and Visitors Authority, State of Nevada,
Subject. /
CORRECTED
REVIEW PANEL DETERMINATION
NRS 281A.730; NAC 281A.440
The Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”) initiated this Ethics Complaint
(“Complaint”) on January 8, 2026, regarding the alleged conduct of Subject Lisa Motley
(“Subject”). On January 8, 2026, the Commission instructed the Executive Director to
investigate alleged violations of NRS 281A.400(1), (2), (3), (5), (9), (10), and NRS
281A.420(1).
Subject is a former public employee as defined in NRS 281A.150 and NRS
281A.180, and the Commission has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to NRS
281A.280 because the allegations contained in the Complaint relate to Subject’s conduct
as a public employee and associated implications under the Ethics Law. Subject did not
waive the statutory investigatory time limit of 70 days.
On March 24, 2026, a Review Panel consisting of Scott Scherer, Esq. (Presiding
Officer), Commissioner Lowry, and Commissioner Moran considered the following: (1)
Ethics Complaint; (2) Order Initiating Complaint by Motion; (3) Motley’s Response; and
(4) Executive Director’s Recommendation to the Review Panel with Summary of
Investigatory Findings and Relevant Evidentiary Exhibits.1
///
///
///
1All materials provided to the Review Panel, except the Ethics Complaint and the Order on Jurisdiction and
Investigation, represent portions of the investigatory file and remain confidential pursuant to NRS 281A.750.
Review Panel Determination
Case No. 26-007C
Page 1 of 2

Under NAC 281A.430, the Panel unanimously finds and concludes that the facts
do not establish credible evidence to support a determination that just and sufficient cause
exists for the Commission to render an opinion in the matter regarding the alleged
violations of NRS 281A.400(1), (2), (3), (9), (10), and NRS 281A.420(1). The Panel further
unanimously finds and concludes that the facts do establish credible evidence to support
a determination that just and sufficient cause exists for the Commission to render an
opinion in the matter regarding the alleged violations of NRS 281A.400(5) and refer the
alleged violation of this statute to the full Commission for an opinion.
DATED this 24th day of March, 2026.
REVIEW PANEL OF THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
